newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's Berisford faces possible bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's Berisford faces possible bid.

text.p: Shares in British consumer food equipment to agri-business group Berisford Plc rode high on Friday after it disclosed it had received a takeover approach and despite reporting a dip in annual pretax profits.
Berisford said it had received a "formal interest" in an offer made for the company.
It said the approach "had been only of a preliminary nature such that it is unclear whether it may or may not lead to an offer being made".
Berisford's share price shot up to 150 pence from Thursday's close of 121 pence after the company announced the approach.
This contrasted with a slight dip in pretax profits.
Berisford's pretax profit for the year ended September 28, 1996 fell to 25.5 million pounds stg ($43 million) from 26.8 million in the previous year.
Analysts covering the company said it would attract a price tag of 175 to 200 pence a share, valuing the company at 300 to 365 million pounds, if the bid offer is launched.
One sector analyst at a British broker said, "At today's earnings, I would see a price of around 200 pence a share."
Analysts who met Berisford management at a meeting called by the company to outline its full year results said executives were tight-lipped over the name of the potential buyer.
But they did say that the company confirmed there was only one potential bidder at present.
Swedish consumer goods manufacturer Electrolux was hotly tipped by analysts as the suitor given its estimated cash reserves of more than 600 million pounds.
The prize jewel in Berisford's crown is its U.S. food manufacturing equipment subsidiary Welbilt Corporation which accounts for nearly 60 percent of its turnover.
"That makes Electrolux a strong contender, given its presence in the U.S.," said another City analyst.
British diversified groups Tomkins Plc and Wassal Plc are also named by analysts as potential buyers.
Analysts said the only factor that could influence the current management to sell was sluggishness in the consumer food equipment industry in the UK and the U.S.

The British sector suffers from overcapacity. In the U.S. some of Welbilt's main clients, the consumer food giants, have failed to expand into mainland Europe and Asia at a pace expected three years ago.
"The sell-off will be influenced by industry constraints," an analyst said.
The company, however, said it had fared better in the first seven weeks of the current financial year with sales and orders at Welbilt rising one and eight percent respectively.
It said sales at its UK-based Magnet unit were up 11 percent, retail kitchen orders were up 19 percent while direct kitchen sales rose eight percent.
Analysts said Electrolux was more likely to make an outright cash purchase, if it launched an offer, while the British firms would probably favour offering shares.
The company said the possible offer made its proposed buy-back of convertible unsecured loan stock impracticable until the situation had been clarified.
